title: How a house foundation is built
caption: What's actually holding your house up 🏠 #howitsbuilt #foundation #construction #homeowner #howitworks

lines.text: If you build a house straight on the dirt, it sinks unevenly and cracks.
So you dig a trench and pour a wide concrete *footing*, which spreads the weight across more ground.
But in winter, wet ground freezes, swells, and lifts anything sitting on it.
So you dig the footing deeper, below the *frost line*, where the ground doesn't freeze.
But concrete is strong when you squeeze it, and weak when you stretch it, so it cracks.
So you run steel *rebar* through it, to hold it together when it pulls apart.
Then you build wooden *forms* on top, and pour the foundation walls.
But concrete soaks up water from the ground, and wood sitting on it would rot.
So the first board, the *sill plate*, is pressure-treated, and sits on a foam strip that seals the gap.
Now you can build the house.
But an earthquake can shake a house sideways, right off its foundation.
So *anchor bolts* set in the concrete reach up through the sill plate, and lock the house down.
But in warm places, termites tunnel up out of the soil to eat the wood.
So you treat the soil, and keep the wood well up off the dirt.
